newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela to meet Netanyahu, Arafat next month.
newsitem.headline: Mandela to meet Netanyahu, Arafat next month.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Thursday he would visit the Middle East as planned next month and tell Israeli and Palestinian leaders to sort out their differences.

"I plan to go and talk to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Yasser Arafat, because whatever problems you have, you reach a stage where none of the parties are totally correct or totally wrong," he said.
"That is the situation which has been reached in the Middle East," he told reporters after meeting the South African Jewish Board of Deputies in Pretoria.

"My message to them is going...to be, 'When historians record what happened in Israel and Palestine they are going to say that the troubles occurred when the two of you were leaders. That will be the indictment of history'."
Fifty-eight Palestinians and 15 Israelis have died in gun battles and clashes since Israel opened a tunnel to archaeological sites near Jerusalem's Temple Mount, sacred to Moslems and Jews.

Mandela's first visit to Israel, Palestinian territories, Jordan and Egypt from November 4 was twice postponed from August and then October, officially in order to lengthen the visit. The government has not said how long the trip will be.
